{{Short description|Mathematical functor}}
{{unreferenced|date=May 2014}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''topological half-exact functor''' ''F'' is a [[functor]] from a fixed topological [[category (mathematics)|category]] (for example [[CW complexes]] or [[pointed space]]s) to an [[abelian category]] (most frequently in applications, category of [[abelian group]]s or category of [[module (mathematics)|modules]] over a fixed ring) that has a following property: for each sequence of spaces, of the form:

: ''X'' → ''Y'' → ''C(f)''

where ''C(f)'' denotes a [[Mapping cone (topology)|mapping cone]], the sequence:

: ''F(X)'' → ''F(Y)'' → ''F(C(f))''

is [[Exact sequence|exact]].  If ''F'' is a contravariant functor, it is '''half-exact''' if for each sequence of spaces as above,
the sequence ''F(C(f))'' → ''F(Y)'' → ''F(X)'' is exact.

[[homology (mathematics)|Homology]] is an example of a half-exact functor, and
[[cohomology]] (and [[generalized cohomology theories]])  are examples of contravariant half-exact functors.
If ''B'' is any fibrant topological space, the (representable) functor ''F(X)=[X,B]'' is half-exact.
